item_name: Passive Electronic Components (Resistors, Capacitors, Inductors, Ferrite Beads)
hazard_level: Low to Moderate (High if old electrolytic or tantalum capacitors leak)
hazards: Lead in older capacitor/resistor terminations and solder
Corrosive chemical electrolytes inside electrolytic capacitors
Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) in rare legacy capacitors
safe_handling: Handle loose components using tweezers or nitrile gloves
Store in sealed, labeled antistatic bags or rigid containers
Avoid inhaling dust from broken ferrite cores
unsafe_actions: Never puncture, crush, or apply direct flame to capacitors (burst risk)
Do not sweep loose components into regular dustbins
Do not wash leaking electrolytes down drains
what_to_do_if_damaged: Avoid bare-skin contact with bulging or leaking capacitors. Wear gloves, wipe residue with a disposable cloth, and seal both the component and cloth in a labeled hazardous e-waste pouch.
disposal_route: Hand over sorted components to an authorized e-waste dismantler/recycler or hazardous waste treatment facility (TSDF) for safe metal and ceramic recovery.
environmental_impact: Tiny loose components easily enter soil and waterways during informal dumping, slowly leaching heavy metals and chemical electrolytes into local ecosystems.
